definitions.explanation: Describes a sweet taste in food or drinks.
Figuratively means being too easy on someone, having naive expectations, or being overly optimistic.

notes:
{甘|あま}い is an i-adjective with both literal (sweet taste) and figurative (lenient, naive) meanings.

FORMS:
- Adverbial: {甘|あま}く
- Negative: {甘|あま}くない
- Past: {甘|あま}かった
- Noun form: {甘|あま}さ (sweetness)

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {甘|あま}い⟦もの→もの：02259_mono⟧: sweets, desserts
- {甘|あま}い⟦{物|もの}→もの：02259_mono⟧⟦{好|ず}き→好き：02355_suki⟧: someone with a sweet tooth
- {甘|あま}⟦{口|くち}→口：00560_kuchi⟧: sweet (taste), as opposed to {辛口|からくち} (dry/spicy)

FIGURATIVE USES:
- ⟦{考|かんが}え→考え：00855_kangae⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{甘|あま}い: naive thinking
- ⟦{自分|じぶん}→自分：02887_jibun⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{甘|あま}い: easy on oneself
- ⟦{子供|こども}→子供：00554_kodomo⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{甘|あま}い: lenient with children
- {甘|あま}い⟦{話|はなし}→話：01496_hanashi⟧: too-good-to-be-true deal

OPPOSITE: ⟦{厳|きび}しい→厳しい：01125_kibishii⟧ (strict), ⟦{辛|から}い→辛い：00638_karai⟧ (spicy, harsh)
